text:
Marta: Heads-up — during the flashv3-int8 canary we just rolled, observed ~45% drop in tokens/sec for the kv-heavy chat workload. $/M tokens jumped from ~$1.15 to ~$1.86. attaching quick profiler snippet and notes.

Alex: Can you paste the profiler output / kernel selection log? curious if it's a switch to a slower paged path.

Marta: pasted below (trimmed):
```
$ rk bench --model redwood/xxx:flashv3-int8 --seq 8192 --batch 8 --kv-cache true
[INFO] Selected kernel: flash_attn2_prefetch
[INFO] Runtime decision: switching -> flash_attn_paged (kv-evict heur)
[PROFILE] tokens/sec: 18.2k (canary)  vs baseline 33.1k
[PROFILE] memcpy bytes (gpu->gpu): 2.4G per 30s
[METRIC] kv_evictions: 22
[METRIC] kernel_switch_count: 7
[METRIC] p95_latency_ms: 320 -> 590
```

Jonathan: That kernel_switch_count looks suspect. Are we throttling prefetch which causes more page faults -> eviction -> fallback?

Marta: My hypothesis: the quantized flashv3-int8 kernel has tighter prefetch memory window. Under the current batching/hysteresis it gets preemptively switched off when the KV working set spikes briefly. That triggers full-kv-copy fallback (paged) which kills throughput and increases memcpy.

Sophia: Could be the hysteresis threshold in kernel_selector: we recently lowered the hysteresis to optimize for short tails. That would make sense. If it oscillates it pays the copy penalty on each switch.

Alex: Repro steps we should run:
1) run long steady-state workload with --trace-kernel-decisions=1
2) simulate KV burst via toy client (open many contexts then issue long generate)
3) capture nvprof on the canary host and compare memcpy/copy counts

Marta: I ran 1 & 2 on canary host g12: attached light nvprof dump (summary):
```
Memcpy HtoD  total 1.9GB  calls 18
Memcpy DtoH  total 2.1GB  calls 21
Kernel flash_attn2_prefetch time 45%
Kernel flash_attn_paged time 40% (post-switch)
```

Kevin: I opened a tiny PR that forces kernel selection to avoid switching for <200ms transient spikes and defers eviction by 50MB: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123

perf-bot: [run 2034567920] perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/dash/kv-burst/2034567920 (canary) :charts: benchmark-suite run id=2034567920

Jonathan: Nice. Also check batching heuristic: when the batcher compacts variable-length requests it can produce denser batches that increase working set suddenly. Might interact badly with prefetch window sizing. Can we instrument batcher to emit working_set_bytes per batch?

Sophia: I'll add a temporary metric batch_working_set_bytes on the canary branch. If we correlate batch spikes with kernel switches we can tune hysteresis/fallback delay.

Marta: Plan for next 24h:
- pin flash_attn2 for canary to stop regressions (quick rollback)
- run extended kv-burst synthetic with nvprof and batcher instrumentation
- roll Kevin's patch into canary and validate tokens/sec and $/M tokens
- if stable, propagate to rollout (A/B)

Alex: For dollars-per-million calc, use tokens/sec * price_per_gpu_hour and normalized tokens per gpu-hour. I can help generate a script to compute $/M from bench outputs.

Marta: Thanks — I'll run baseline vs patch and paste $/M numbers here. Current canary: $/M =~ $1.86. baseline pinned flash_attn2: $/M =~ $1.13. Need to get patch into canary before any further rollout.

Kevin: small note — the patch also guards against kernel switch during active kv-eviction operation to avoid mid-copy switches. should reduce memcpy churn.

Jonathon: ack, I'm on nvprof correlation and will post artifacts (flamegraphs + kernel timeline) when done.

Marta: TL;DR: regression caused by oscillating kernel selection + KV eviction -> extra memcpy + paged fallback. Mitigation: pin kernel + tune hysteresis + defer eviction. PR up (4123) + canary instrumentation in flight.

Sophia: :thumbsup: keep us posted, will prepare config rollout knobs for Dedicated pools too.

Kevin: pushing patch to canary now.

perf-bot: deploy event: canary updated with runtime@patch-4123 at 2034567925

Marta: confirming new canary run (2034567920) shows tokens/sec back to ~31.5k and $/M tokens down to ~$1.22. continuing longer run for stability.

Alex: great, if stable let's add a longer hysteresis as a permanent fix and add a perf test to catch this next time.

Marta: Agreed. I'll open follow-up ticket to add a regression test in benchmark-suite and a dashboard alert for kernel_switch_count > 3/min per host.

Kevin: thanks everyone.
